links.outcome: Diagnostic alignment and treatment decisions in health-worker plans with versus without LLM feedback, judged by on-site physicians
links.effect: Health workers changed prescribing for more than half of patients, but on-site physicians saw little to no improvement; lab tests showed mixed effects with no significant increase in detection rates.
links.quote: However, on-site physicians observed little to no improvement in diagnostic alignment or treatment decisions.

links.outcome: Agreement between chart-based retrospective review and on-site real-world clinical evaluation of LLM-assisted plans
links.effect: Retrospective academic reviewers rated LLM-assisted plans more favorably, while on-site physicians and laboratory tests showed little to no improvement, revealing a gap between chart review and real-world relevance.
links.quote: This highlights a gap between chart-based reviews and real-world clinical relevance that may be especially important in evaluating the effectiveness of LLM-based interventions.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating LLM decision support against laboratory test results as objective ground truth
Comparing chart-based retrospective review with on-site physician assessment of the same patients

screen.reason: Empirical real-world deployment evaluating the impact of providing LLM decision support feedback to health workers on clinical plans, compared to unassisted plans.

primary.practice: LLM decision support feedback on care plans
